To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FO MBR can effectively treat the effluent from AnMBR, and the membrane fouling in FO MBR treating effluent from atmospheric AnMBR was more serious than that from mesophilic AnMBr.
the flux decline in FO membrane bioreactor was affected by the quantity of organic foulants in the external and internal foulants.
the FO membrane processes could effectively remove N and P from the effluents of mesophilic and atmospheric AnMBRs, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of membrane fouling on the performance of FO MBRs treating AnMBR effluent.
the effect of operating temperature on the membrane fouling in the FO process, which provides a new insight to the application of FO process in wastewater treatment.
the application of FO process for treating the effluent of AnMBRs and the characteristics of organic membrane foulant in FOMBRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane fouling in FO processes was not only related to membrane foulants, but also related to membrane fouling mechanisms.
the membrane fouling was mainly caused by the accumulation of organic matter on the surface of membrane in P-FOMB, while the membrane fouling in M-FOMB was mainly caused by pore fouling.

the flux decline in FO membrane process is mainly caused by the adsorption and deposition of organic matter into membrane pores, and the accumulation of protein-like foulants in FO membrane pores is not the main reason for membrane fouling in the FO membrane process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FO membrane fouling was more serious when the FO membrane was operated at higher temperature.
the FO process is suitable for treating AnMBR effluent and the membrane fouling in FO processes is related to the characteristics of organic foulants.
the FO membrane fouling behavior was not only related to the accumulation of external foulants, but also related to the adsorption of internal foulants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the FO process can improve the nutrient removal efficiencies of AnMBR effluents, and the flux decline of FO membrane in the FOMBRs is mainly caused by the accumulation of protein-like compounds into external foulants and the deposition or adsorption of organic matter into FO membrane pores.

the organic foulants in FO processes are mainly composed of protein-like substances and the quantity of organic fouling in FO membrane pores is a key factor to determine the membrane fouling in the FO process.

the membrane fouling in FO processes was not simply related to the accumulation of organic membrane foulant into external foulants, which was also influenced by the quantity of organic foulant depositing into membrane pores.
